title: Trends in Maternal Care
context: Source: Report Page 26.
analysis: Positive trends are observed across all maternal health indicators. Skilled Birth Attendance improved significantly from 43% in 2018 to 52.4% in 2024, reflecting improved access to obstetric care.

title: Antenatal Care (4+)
context: Source: Page 24.
analysis: The South West (88.9%) and South East (86.4%) maintain high ANC coverage. However, the North West (30.1%) indicates that 70% of women in this zone do not receive the recommended number of antenatal visits.

title: Institutional Delivery
context: Source: Page 24.
analysis: A sharp disparity exists: 90% of births in the South West occur in facilities, compared to only 20% in the North West. This correlates strongly with maternal mortality risks.

title: Skilled Birth Attendance
context: Source: Page 24.
analysis: Skilled assistance at delivery is highest in the South West (92.3%). The low rate in the North West (24.8%) highlights a critical need for more skilled health workers in northern rural communities.

title: Difficulty walking or climbing steps
context: Percentage of population age 5+ with difficulty walking or climbing steps
analysis: Nationally, 4.1% of the population age 5 + have some level of difficulty walking or climbing steps. The prevalence is generally higher in the North Central and North East zones compared to the Southern zones.

title: Men Financial Inclusion
context: Percentage of men who use bank accounts or mobile money
analysis: Nationally, 57% of men who use bank accounts or mobile money. There are significant regional disparities, generally with higher rates in the South compared to the North.

title: Women Participate in Household Decisions
context: Percentage of married women who participate in all three household decisions
analysis: Nationally, 36% of married women who participate in all three household decisions. There are significant regional disparities, generally with higher rates in the South compared to the North.

title: Access to Basic Drinking Water
context: Percentage of population with at least basic drinking water service
analysis: At the national level, 70.5% of the population has with at least basic drinking water service. Access levels are generally better in urban areas and Southern zones compared to rural areas and Northern zones.

title: Teenage Pregnancy
context: Source: Table 5, Page 14. Percentage of women age 15-19 who have ever been pregnant.
analysis: Nationally, 15% of teenage women have ever been pregnant. The rate is highest in the North West (22.5%) and lowest in the South East (5.2%). State variations are significant, ranging from 2.6% in Edo to 31.6% in Kebbi.

title: Improved Water Source
context: Percentage of population using an improved drinking water source
analysis: At the national level, 75.6% of the population has using an improved drinking water source. Access levels are generally better in urban areas and Southern zones compared to rural areas and Northern zones.

context: Percentage of households with water available on premises
analysis: At the national level, 37.6% of the population has percentage of households with water available on premises. Access levels are generally better in urban areas and Southern zones compared to rural areas and Northern zones.

title: Access to Basic Sanitation
context: Percentage of population with at least basic sanitation service
analysis: At the national level, 49.1% of the population has with at least basic sanitation service. Access levels are generally better in urban areas and Southern zones compared to rural areas and Northern zones.

title: Total Fertility Rate
context: Source: Table 3, Page 11. The average number of children a woman would have by the end of her childbearing years.
analysis: The TFR is 4.8 children per woman nationally. Rural areas (5.6) have significantly higher fertility than urban areas (3.9). The North East zone (6.1) has the highest TFR, while the South West (3.4) has the lowest.

title: Median Age at First Birth
context: Source: Table 6, Page 16. Age by which half of women have had their first child.
analysis: The national median age at first birth is 21.3 years. Urban women tend to have their first child later (22.9 years) than rural women (20.6 years), reflecting differences in education and economic opportunities.

title: Desire for Children
context: Source: Table 7, Page 16. Fertility preferences among currently married women age 15-49.
analysis: 28% of married women want another child soon (within 2 years), while 33% want another child later. 27% want no more children, indicating a significant unmet need for family planning services.

title: Trends in Fertility
context: Source: Figure 1, Page 12. Change in TFR over time.
analysis: The TFR has declined from 6.3 in 1990 to 4.8 in 2023-24. Rural areas consistently show higher fertility than urban areas, though both have declined over time.

title: Age-Specific Fertility Rates
context: Source: Table 3, Page 11. Births per 1,000 women by age group.
analysis: Fertility is low among adolescents (77 births per 1,000 women age 15-19), peaks at 233 births per 1,000 among women age 25-29, and then decreases thereafter. Rural areas show consistently higher fertility rates across all age groups compared to urban areas.
